definition: A CubeSat built from six standardized units. NASA lists nominal dimensions of 100 × 226.3 × 366 mm for the 6U structure.
An orbit relatively close to Earth. EarthWatch-1 uses 500 km as its selected educational scenario altitude.
Collecting information about Earth's surface, atmosphere, or environment using sensors and imaging instruments.
Equipment that performs the main mission task. EarthWatch-1 uses an Earth-observation camera as its example payload.
Solar cells connected into panels or arrays that convert sunlight into electrical power.
The maximum power rating under specified conditions. It is not the same as average power available throughout an orbit.
Power averaged over a stated period. For a satellite it depends on sunlight, eclipse, orientation, and operating schedule.
The amount of electrical charge a battery can store, commonly expressed in ampere-hours (Ah).
Stored electrical energy, commonly expressed in watt-hours (Wh). It depends on both battery capacity and voltage.
The subsystem that determines and controls the spacecraft's orientation.
A ground-based facility used to communicate with a spacecraft.
Transmission of data from a spacecraft to a ground station.
The allocation and accounting of spacecraft mass, including a margin for growth and uncertainty.
An accounting of electrical power generated, stored, and consumed by spacecraft subsystems.
A chosen simplified value used to make the educational game playable. It must not be described as a verified hardware specification.
A reference condition near the start of a spacecraft's operational life; solar-array output can change over time due to degradation and operating conditions.
